For each family, we select three expert models specializing in mathematics, coding, and instruction following, respectively. Specifically, for the Llama-3 family, we use math expert models Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct _ \_ math and coding expert models Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct _ \_ coding from MergeBench (He et al., 2025 ) as the two expert models, and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct as the instruction-following expert. Following Chakraborty et al. ( 2025 ) , we use the reward model Ray2333/reward-model-Mistral-7B-instruct-Unified-Feedback as the external reward for Collab (Chakraborty et al., 2025 ) . For the Gemma-2 family, we use Gemma-2-2B-Instruct _ \_ math , Gemma-2-2B-Instruct _ \_ coding and Gemma-2-2B-Instruct _ \_ instruction from MergeBench (He et al., 2025 ) as three expert models. For a fair comparison, we use weqweasdas/RM-Gemma-2B as the external reward for Collab (Chakraborty et al., 2025 ) , instead of a larger 7B reward model. We randomly select 500 samples from the PerfectBlend dataset (Xu et al., 2024 ) as a held-out test set and use the remaining samples as the training pool. For the initial SFT phase, we randomly sample 200k examples from the PerfectBlend training split, which provides a balanced mixture of mathematics, coding, and instruction-following tasks.
